issues.description: The problem statement gives conflicting instructions about the SealSaloon.stock attribute: one section (requesting initialization in the constructor as a final instance field) implies an instance (non-static) field, while a later note explicitly requires the stock attribute to be static and shared across all SealSaloon instances. This contradiction will confuse students about whether to implement stock as an instance field initialized in the constructor or as a static class field.
issues.suggestedFix: Clarify the specification: decide whether stock should be an instance final field initialized in the constructor or a static shared field. Update problem_statement.md to consistently state the chosen design. If the intended design is a shared stock, revise the earlier sentence about initializing 'stock' in the constructor to indicate class-level (static) initialization; if the intended design is instance-level, remove the note requiring stock to be static and adjust related method requirements.

issues.description: The problem UML and solution expect a StockIngredient constructor with signature StockIngredient(String, int, int), but the provided template only offers a constructor with four parameters (String, int, int, boolean strictValidation). This mismatch prevents students from constructing StockIngredient objects with the expected three-argument constructor as shown in the problem and solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Add an overloaded three-argument constructor StockIngredient(String name, int price, int quantity) to the template StockIngredient class (or change the existing constructor signature back to the three-argument form). Implement it to delegate to the existing logic or perform equivalent validation so students can create StockIngredient instances using the expected signature.

issues.description: The problem statement and the solution expect a StockIngredient constructor with three parameters StockIngredient(String, int, int), but the template implementation provides a constructor with an extra boolean parameter (StockIngredient(String, int, int, boolean)). This API mismatch (constructor signature) prevents students from mapping the described/expected constructor to the template code and may cause compilation or usage confusion when creating StockIngredient instances as shown in the problem examples.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the template API with the problem statement and solution by providing a StockIngredient(String, int, int) constructor in the template (either replace the 4-parameter constructor or add an overloaded 3-parameter constructor that delegates to the strict variant). This ensures students can instantiate StockIngredient objects as described in the task and match the solution's usage.
